claims.claim: Wizards of the Coast's own 2024 settlement handout bands settlement size by population, with a village at up to 500 people.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, Settlement Tracker handout, 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide

claims.claim: The same 2024 handout sets the town band at a population of 501 to 5,000.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, Settlement Tracker handout, 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide

claims.claim: The same 2024 handout sets the city band at a population of 5,001 or more.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, Settlement Tracker handout, 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide

claims.claim: The publisher's settlement slot list opens with a slot labelled Defining Trait.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, Settlement Tracker handout, 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide

claims.claim: The publisher's settlement slot list carries a slot labelled Claim to Fame.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, Settlement Tracker handout, 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide

claims.claim: The publisher's settlement slot list carries a single leadership slot labelled Local Leader.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, Settlement Tracker handout, 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide

claims.claim: The publisher's settlement handout keeps a list slot for the settlement's noteworthy places, separate from its people.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, Settlement Tracker handout, 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide

claims.claim: The only economic figure the publisher's settlement handout asks a DM to record is the gp value of the most expensive item for sale.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, Settlement Tracker handout, 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide
claims.quote: GP VALUE OF THE MOST EXPENSIVE ITEM FOR SALE

claims.claim: The Death House read-aloud paragraph opens a settlement with a road, the village, and a simile drawn from its own building stock rather than with any statistic.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, Death House (Curse of Strahd introductory adventure), 2016
claims.quote: The gravel road leads to a village, its tall houses dark as

claims.claim: Death House names a building by the name the locals give it rather than by an owner or address.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast, Death House (Curse of Strahd introductory adventure), 2016
claims.quote: Death House is the name given to an old row house

claims.claim: D&D Beyond's own launch article says the 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide's handouts serve as a template for building settlements.
claims.source: Mike Bernier, 'What's New in the 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide?', D&D Beyond, 12 Nov 2024

claims.claim: Wizards of the Coast states that the 2024 Dungeon Master's Guide replaces all rules in the 2014 version of the book.
claims.source: DND Staff, 'Updates in the Dungeon Master's Guide (2024)', D&D Beyond, 20 Feb 2025
claims.quote: it replaces all rules in the 2014 version of the book

claims.claim: An official free D&D Beyond encounter opens a settlement entry with the settlement's name, a population figure, and its people's trade, in one sentence.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Snowed In', 2020
claims.quote: Icehaven is a village of 5,000 souls

claims.claim: The same official column calls Icehaven a village while giving it a population of 5,000, a figure the publisher's own 2024 settlement handout places in the town band.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Snowed In', 2020
claims.quote: Icehaven is a village of 5,000 souls

claims.claim: The same column names a settlement's leader as office title plus given name plus surname, in that order.
claims.source: Wizards of the Coast / D&D Beyond, 'Encounter of the Week: Snowed In', 2020
claims.quote: The leader of the village, Starosta Ernath Noack
